$comment: Super primitives: a named action that fires a group of lower-level body-part moves on an intended schedule, where every step carries the sensor reading that decides whether it actually happened. The schedule and the acceptance criterion belong together -- a grasp is not 'the fingers reached these angles', it is 'the thumb was loaded before the fingers closed'. Splitting those apart is how a hand that formed a perfect shape around nothing got reported as a grasp.

sensor_kinds.none: The step is a positioning move with nothing to verify yet.
sensor_kinds.force: Contact normal force on named digits, read from the simulated contacts. This is the finger's own sense of touch: it can only report a load that actually existed.
sensor_kinds.vision: Where the head was looking and how far off-axis, read from the compiled gaze. A step that cannot be seen cannot be visually verified, and says so rather than passing by default.

grab.description: Power grasp: the object is enclosed between the digits and the palm.

steps.label: open
steps.note: Positioning only. No contact is expected, and a contact here means the approach swept through the object instead of around it.

steps.label: preshape
steps.note: The object must be in view before the hand commits to a shape for it.

steps.label: thumb_anchor
steps.note: The thumb must be loaded FIRST. Index and middle reaching a free object before the thumb push it out of the hand, which is the specific failure this ordering exists to prevent.

steps.label: close_fingers
steps.note: At least two opposing fingers loaded while the thumb anchor holds.

steps.label: secure
steps.note: Enough load, on enough digits, in opposition, to carry the object's weight through a lift.

pinch.description: Precision grasp: thumb pad against index pad, the rest clear.

steps.label: open
steps.note: Positioning only. No contact is expected: a load here means the pads closed before they were around anything, which for a pinch is a poke.

steps.label: approach_pads
steps.note: A pinch is small and the head must be watching the hand, not the object: at this scale the difference between contact and near-miss is not visible from the object's centre.

steps.label: pad_contact
steps.note: Both pads loaded and opposed. A pinch with one pad loaded is a poke.

steps.label: secure
steps.note: Lower force than a power grasp on purpose: a precision grasp that squeezes like a power grasp crushes what it is holding.

release.description: Open every digit and give the object up.

steps.label: held
steps.note: Releasing presupposes holding. A release that starts with nothing in the hand did not happen.

steps.label: clear
steps.note: No digit still loaded. The inverse criterion: this step passes on the ABSENCE of force.
